title: Discharging preserves the total charge
notes: Assign charge \(60(6-i)\) to degree i, redistribute 30 along specified edges, and seek a contradiction by making every final charge nonpositive.
statement: The initial charge sum is \(720\). Any pairwise transfer conserves it. Therefore, if absence of a finite configuration family forces every final charge to be nonpositive under a fully specified set of transfer rules, that family is unavoidable. The single sample rule in the notes does not by itself prove the required universal implication.
reconstruction: Conservation is exact; completeness of the discharge rules is not reconstructed from the incomplete examples.
fate: \citet[\S3, discharging steps 1--2]{gonthier2005fourcolour} gives the precise proof pattern. Appel--Haken's completed rule system is a much larger object than this board sketch. For the manuscript computer-time question, the contemporary digest \citet[abstract]{bernhart1977digest} reports 1200 hours for nearly 1900 configurations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Zero microsupport detects local constancy
notes: \(SS(F)\) equals the zero section iff all cohomology sheaves are locally constant; the whole zero section is again inserted for any nonzero complex.
statement: For a constructible complex, \(SS(F)\subset T_X^*X\) iff all its cohomology sheaves are locally constant. Equality holds on connected components where the complex is nonzero. The zero complex has empty support, so equality cannot be used without the component/support qualification.
fate: \citet[\S3.1]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} gives the local-constancy criterion. This is a second occurrence of the support error corrected in 1987-744.3.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Vanishing cycles as relative hypercohomology
notes: Take \(f(x)=0\), \(df_x=\nu\), and compare cohomology on a small neighbourhood with a nearby nonzero fibre; relative cohomology is defined by a cone.
statement: For a sufficiently small Milnor neighbourhood and a constructible complex adapted to \(f\), the relative derived sections \(R\Gamma(B,B\cap f^{-1}(\varepsilon);F)\) are the fibre of the restriction map. Equivalently they are its cone shifted by \(-1\). They describe local vanishing-cycle data, with the chosen convention recorded.
reconstruction: The Milnor neighbourhood, nearby regular value and shifted-cone convention are supplied.
fate: The microlocal construction in \citet[\S1]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal} uses these local Morse data. The cone shift matters for the degree-zero definition on the next line.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Repeated microlocal characterization of perversity
notes: A holomorphic Morse function has graph transverse to singular support; vanishing cycles occur in one degree and form a local system over the smooth support.
statement: Use isolated transverse intersections with the smooth support, degree-zero normalized Morse groups, and the Maslov-twisted local-system construction. These are the same conditions as in 1987-744.7--744.11, not a new criterion.
reconstruction: The normalization and twist from the earlier occurrence remain necessary.
fate: \citet[Theorem~9.5.2]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} and \citet[\S1]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal} supply the precise formulations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Reconstruct perverse sheaves from microlocal Morse data
notes: The proposed third method is a microlocal description by vanishing cycles; the report says the work solves half of the problem.
statement: Let \(X\) be a complex manifold and \(\Lambda\subset T^*X\) a specified closed complex analytic conic Lagrangian. With coefficients in \(\mathbb C\), describe the category of perverse sheaves with singular support in \(\Lambda\) by local Morse data on the smooth pieces, gluing at codimension-one loci, and explicit compatibility conditions at singular loci. A complete answer must characterize the essential image, not only embed the category faithfully.
reconstruction: The fixed-support categorical formulation and essential-image distinction make the informal reconstruction question precise; no arbitrary missing codimension-two formula is invented.
fate: \citet[Theorem~5.1 and Theorem~6.4]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal}, first circulated on arXiv in September 2005, proves an equivalence away from the codimension-two locus and a global fully faithful embedding in melded Morse data. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{kashiwaravilonen2014codimension}, announced in 2010 with a full preprint in 2012 and publication in 2014, proves unique extension across analytic subsets of codimension at least three in the Lagrangian support. The exact remaining task is formulated as Problem~9.3 of that paper (published p.~617): describe the conditions imposed by the codimension-two locus on the essential image. The extension theorem does not erase these conditions. \citet[Introduction]{guminov2025perverse} confirms that explicit category descriptions remain available only for restricted families.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: partially developed over complex coefficients in the explicit microlocal-data sense stated here. Kashiwara--Vilonen Problem 9.3 explicitly isolates the codimension-two essential-image question. The consulted later primary literature does not settle that general geometric description; this is a bounded search conclusion, not a claim that no categorical reconstruction theorem of any kind exists.
worth: A fixed singular support with concrete codimension-two links would make a useful bounded project, but the notebook supplies no such geometry to calculate here.

title: Holonomic differential equations and perverse solution complexes
notes: One construction uses overdetermined differential equations, a solution complex, and a Dolbeault resolution.
statement: For a regular holonomic left \(\mathcal D_X\)-module on a smooth complex n-fold, the shifted derived solution complex \(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(M,\mathcal O_X)[n]\) is perverse. Regular holonomic modules and complex-constructible perverse sheaves correspond contravariantly. A merely overdetermined system need not be holonomic, and an ordinary solution sheaf need not equal its derived solution complex.
reconstruction: Regular holonomicity is used for this safe exact equivalence; the notebook does not specify the module class or solution shift.
fate: \citet[main theorem, p.~1]{kashiwara1980constructible} announces the derived equivalence in the lecture of 22 April 1980; \citet{kashiwara1984riemann} is the full later publication. This predates the seminar.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Intersection cohomology and intermediate extension
notes: The Goresky--MacPherson combinatorial method extends sheaves to singular points and yields perverse sheaves.
statement: If \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) is a smooth dense stratum of complex dimension d and \(L\) a finite-rank local system, its perverse intermediate extension \(j_{!*}L[d]\) is the intersection-cohomology complex. Arbitrary extensions across singular strata need not be perverse or canonical.
reconstruction: Intermediate extension is the precise reconstruction of the broad extension statement.
fate: The intersection-cohomology construction is \citet{goreskymacpherson1983intersection}; the extension viewpoint is also explicit in \citet{beilinson1987glue}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The finite Morse index of a geodesic
notes: The energy functional on the path space has finite negative index, equal to the number of conjugate points along the geodesic.
statement: For a geodesic segment in a smooth Riemannian manifold with fixed endpoints, the Hessian of energy has finite Morse index. It equals the sum of the multiplicities of conjugate points to the initial endpoint in the open segment; conjugacy at the final endpoint contributes to nullity, not to the negative index.
reconstruction: Fixed endpoints and the endpoint/nullity convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S\S1--3]{duistermaat1974morse} formulates the index in variational and Lagrangian terms. Boundary conditions and multiplicities, omitted in the board sentence, determine the exact result.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Relative grading for strongly indefinite functionals
notes: Critical points may have infinitely many positive and negative directions, but the numbers of negative directions are said to differ by a finite number; homology is counted from infinity over two.
statement: For a continuous path of self-adjoint Fredholm Hessians with invertible ends and appropriate operator-domain control, spectral flow supplies a finite relative index. Infinite positive and negative indices alone do not imply that an index difference exists. A Floer complex additionally requires compactness, transversality, coherent orientation and control of broken trajectories.
reconstruction: The Fredholm and analytic hypotheses replace subtraction of two infinite cardinalities.
fate: \citet[pp.~286--294]{atiyah1988invariants} explains the gauge-theoretic Morse picture, circulated as a 1987 lecture/preprint. \citet{floer1988instanton}, received 3 May and published June 1988, establishes the associated homology-sphere invariant. This is exposition of a programme under development, not a general theorem for arbitrary functionals.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: relative-index Floer theories are established under specific analytic hypotheses; the unrestricted formulation is invalid.

title: Relation with Donaldson invariants
notes: The striking claim is that these invariants are related to Donaldson invariants of four-manifolds; gauge fields and flat connections are drawn.
statement: The relevant functional on three-dimensional connections is Chern--Simons: its critical points are flat connections and its cylinder gradient equation is the anti-self-dual equation in four dimensions. Donaldson theory can therefore interact with the boundary Floer groups through cutting and gluing.
reconstruction: The functional is reconstructed as Chern--Simons from the named source and later continuation; Yang--Mills criticality alone would be insufficient.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--5]{atiyah1988invariants} is the named source; record 751 supplies the detailed seminar continuation. The ordinary Yang--Mills energy on a three-manifold can have nonflat critical points, so the functional in the sketch must not be identified with it without correction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Positive and negative Fourier polarizations on the circle
notes: Gelfand recalls decomposing \(C^\infty(S^1)\) into boundary values extending inside and outside, with applications to tau-functions and semi-infinite cohomology.
statement: A smooth complex function on the circle splits into its Fourier modes \(\sum_{n\geq0}a_nz^n\) and \(\sum_{n<0}a_nz^n\). With constants included in both pieces the intersection is one-dimensional; with the negative part vanishing at infinity the direct-sum convention removes that overlap. Appropriate Sobolev completions give Hardy polarizations.
reconstruction: Boundary regularity, the constant mode and the outside normalization are made explicit.
fate: The elementary Fourier construction verifies the concrete circle example. \citet[the loop-space discussion]{atiyah1988invariants} supplies the context of relative polarizations; no new tau-function identity is asserted.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Replacing the circle by another manifold
notes: Gelfand says that remarkably the circle can be replaced by other manifolds, and postpones the explanation.
statement: No definite generalization is determined without a chosen operator or polarization, coefficient bundle, function space and intended semi-infinite invariant.

title: The rank-one quantum enveloping algebra and its completion
notes:
The generators \(H,X^\pm\) satisfy
\[
 [H,X^\pm]=\pm2X^\pm,\qquad
 [X^+,X^-]=\frac{\sinh(hH/2)}{\sinh(h/2)},
\]
with \(q=e^h\); powers of both \(H\) and \(q^{H/4}\) are called a vector-space basis.
statement: One coherent formulation is the h-adic algebra \(U_h(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\), topologically free over \(\mathbb C[[h]]\), with the displayed relations and PBW monomials \((X^-)^aH^b(X^+)^c\). Alternatively, for a numerical generic parameter use the algebraic Cartan generator \(K^{\pm1}\) and a PBW basis in \(X^-,K,X^+\). Exponentials are interpreted in a completion, not added as unspecified independent formal generators.
reconstruction: The completion and base ring are fixed explicitly; the notebook does not specify which algebra is meant by its basis.
fate: \citet[I, Definition~1.1 and Theorem~1.1]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} gives the close publication match. Its series number is E-4-87 but the scanned imprint is 1988; the June 1987 recommendation does not by itself establish first public circulation. Independently, \citet[Example~6.2, p.~807]{drinfeld1987quantum}, a 1986 congress report published in 1987, gives the completed quantum enveloping algebra and symmetric coproduct.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The symmetric coproduct and counit
notes: \(\Delta H=H\otimes1+1\otimes H\), \(\Delta X^\pm=X^\pm\otimes q^{H/4}+q^{-H/4}\otimes X^\pm\); this is an algebra homomorphism and coassociative.
statement: Put \(L=e^{hH/4}\), so \(\Delta L=L\otimes L\). The displayed coproduct extends to the completed algebra, is coassociative, and has counit \(\epsilon(H)=\epsilon(X^\pm)=0\), \(\epsilon(1)=1\).
reconstruction: All tensor products use the same h-adic completion.
fate: These formulas are \citet[I, Theorem~1.1, equations~(1.4)--(1.5)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}. Coassociativity on \(X\) follows by expanding both sides as \(X\otimes L\otimes L+L^{-1}\otimes X\otimes L+L^{-1}\otimes L^{-1}\otimes X\). The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[Example~6.2, p.~807]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The antipode needs a minus sign and half the exponent
notes: The scan states \(S(X^\pm)=q^{H/2}X^\pm q^{-H/2}\), with \(S(H)=-H\).
statement: For the displayed coproduct, \(S(X^\pm)=-L X^\pm L^{-1}=-q^{\pm1/2}X^\pm\), where \(L=q^{H/4}\). Indeed \(m(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta X=S(X)L+LX=0\). The source expression fails this identity and has the wrong classical limit.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{}
fate: \citet[I, Theorem~1.1, equation~(1.6), with \(\rho=H/2\)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} confirms the normalization. The correction is to a faithfully transcribed formula.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the corrected antipode is established; the printed one is incompatible with the printed coproduct.

title: The Cartan-generator substitution changes the denominator
notes: After putting \(K=q^{H/2}\), the notes keep \(KX^\pm=q^{\pm1}X^\pm K\), but write the commutator denominator \(q-q^{-1}\).
statement: With the unchanged parameter \(q=e^h\), the initial relation becomes \([X^+,X^-]=(K-K^{-1})/(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\). If instead the standard parameter is \(t=q^{1/2}\), then \(KX^\pm=t^{\pm2}X^\pm K\) and the denominator is \(t-t^{-1}\). A rescaling of generators is another possible convention, but must be stated.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The correction keeps the original generators and parameter; no silent rescaling is made.
fate: Compare the fixed relation in \citet[I, equation~(1.2)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}. Direct substitution detects the factor mismatch.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Finite-dimensional spin representations and the classical limit
notes: \((X^+)^*=X^-\), \(H^*=H\), and a square-root formula is given on \(e_m^j\), with dimension \(2j+1\); Gelfand asks for the \(q=1\) limit.
statement: For real \(q>0\), define \([a]=(q^{a/2}-q^{-a/2})/(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\), with its limiting value at 1. For \(j\in\frac12\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), \(m=-j,-j+1,\ldots,j\), let \(He_m=2me_m\) and \(X^\pm e_m=\sqrt{[j\mp m][j\pm m+1]}e_{m\pm1}\). These give the compact real-form spin modules and tend to the usual \(\mathfrak{su}_2\) formulas as \(q\to1\).
reconstruction: Nonnegative half-integer j, unit steps for m, and a positive real parameter for the unitary interpretation are restored.
fate: The highest-weight framework is \citet[I, Propositions~1.1--1.2]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}; the rank-one coefficients can be checked by substitution into the relations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Expanding vector fields on the sphere
notes: Gelfand asks how to expand vector fields on a sphere in spherical harmonics, beginning with \(SU(2)\). The last word is partly unclear.
statement: For the standard oriented round \(S^2\), a smooth tangent field is expanded in \(\nabla_{S^2}Y_{\ell m}\) and \(n\times\nabla_{S^2}Y_{\ell m}\), \(\ell\geq1\). There is no harmonic one-form term because \(H^1(S^2)=0\). For an ambient \(\mathbb R^3\)-valued field also include the radial terms \(nY_{\ell m}\). Smooth expansions converge in the smooth topology with the usual coefficient decay.
reconstruction: The standard round sphere and tangent/ambient distinction are supplied; they are not explicit in the abbreviated question.
fate: The scalar normalization is given in \citet[\S14.30]{nist2026dlmf}; gradient and rotated-gradient components follow from the Hodge decomposition on the sphere. This answers a classical exercise, not a new quantum-group problem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The universal R series needs deformation factors and a completion
notes: The formula has \(R=e^{hH\otimes H/4}\sum_{n\geq0}q^n e^n\otimes f^n/[n]_q!\), with \(e=q^{H/4}X^+\), \(f=q^{-H/4}X^-\).
statement: The formal quasitriangular structure has \(R\in U_h\widehat\otimes U_h\), \(R\equiv1\pmod h\), and intertwines the two coproducts. Its nth nilpotent term contains a factor vanishing to order n in h, conventionally a power of \(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2}\). The printed series with the printed e,f cannot have the required classical limit.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The exact missing coefficient is not guessed; only the required deformation order and completion are asserted.
fate: \citet[I, Theorems~1.2--1.3]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} and \citet[\S3]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} give the quasitriangular construction. The q-exponent depends on generator conventions; this chapter does not invent an exact corrected coefficient from the abbreviated series. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S13, pp.~816--817]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Quasitriangular identities and the Yang--Baxter equation
notes: The intertwining equation and Yang--Baxter equation are stated, but both coproduct-factor identities have their order reversed.
statement: With \(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(a)=R\Delta(a)R^{-1}\), use \((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})R=R_{13}R_{23}\), \((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)R=R_{13}R_{12}\). These imply \(R_{12}R_{13}R_{23}=R_{23}R_{13}R_{12}\). Opposite conventions require changing the accompanying definitions consistently.
reconstruction: The correction fixes the intertwining convention already printed in the notes.
fate: The stated order is exactly \citet[I, Theorem~1.3, equations~(1.8a)--(1.8c)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}, also \citet[equations~(3.1.1)--(3.1.3)]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon}. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S10, equations~(20)--(21)]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).

title: The q-gamma function
notes: After the q-factorial definition Gelfand asks what \(\Gamma_q\) is.
statement: For \(0<q<1\), \(\Gamma_q(z)=(1-q)^{1-z}(q;q)_\infty/(q^z;q)_\infty\), with \((a;q)_\infty=\prod_{r\geq0}(1-aq^r)\). It satisfies \(\Gamma_q(z+1)=(1-q^z)\Gamma_q(z)/(1-q)\), \(\Gamma_q(1)=1\), and tends to \(\Gamma(z)\) as \(q\uparrow1\) away from poles.
reconstruction: The choice \(0<q<1\) and the nonsymmetric q-factorial convention make the exercise precise.
fate: The standard q-gamma definition and recurrence are tabulated in \citet[\S5.18, equations~(5.18.4)--(5.18.7)]{nist2026dlmf}. The symmetric q-number in the preceding quantum algebra differs by an elementary q-power normalization.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Braiding and braid-group representations
notes: \(R^{j_1j_2}=P(\pi_{j_1}\otimes\pi_{j_2})(R)\), mapping the tensor factors in the opposite order, satisfies the braid relation.
statement: For finite-dimensional modules in the chosen quasitriangular category, \(c_{V,W}=P\circ(\pi_V\otimes\pi_W)(R)\) is a natural module isomorphism \(V\otimes W\to W\otimes V\). Adjacent c operators on a repeated tensor power obey the braid relations and define a braid-group representation.
reconstruction: On differently coloured strands one has a coloured braid-groupoid action; an ordinary braid group acts on a fixed repeated tensor power.
fate: \citet[I, \S1]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} supplies the R-matrix framework; \citet[\S\S3--5]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} formalizes the graphical functor. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S10, pp.~811--812]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Generic Clebsch--Gordan decomposition
notes: All finite-dimensional representations are called completely reducible, and the tensor product is the classical spin sum.
statement: For a generic parameter, restricted to finite-dimensional type-1 modules, \(V^{j_1}\otimes V^{j_2}\simeq\bigoplus_{r=0}^{2\min(j_1,j_2)}V^{j_1+j_2-r}\). This category is semisimple. Root-of-unity representation categories need not be semisimple, so the omitted parameter restriction changes the theorem.
reconstruction: Generic q and type-1 are specified, and the summation proceeds in steps of one.
fate: \citet[I, Propositions~1.1--1.2 and Theorem~1.5]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} gives the highest-weight and tensor-product setting. The seminar's Clebsch--Gordan coefficients are change-of-basis matrices for this decomposition.

title: Graphical tensor calculus, duality, and ribbon structure
notes: Composition joins diagrams; straight strands denote identities, crossings R and its inverse, and cups/caps have signed q-weight formulas.
statement: In a rigid braided tensor category, composition and tensor product are represented by stacking and juxtaposition. Evaluation and coevaluation must satisfy the two zigzag identities; a ribbon twist supplies compatibility with framed isotopy. Explicit cup/cap coefficients depend on chosen identifications with duals and bases, particularly for half-integer spins.
reconstruction: The categorical identities are identified precisely; no unique phase normalization is inferred from the fragmentary coefficients.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--5]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} proves the precise ribbon-graph functor. Reshetikhin's 1987-numbered LOMI preprints (1988 imprint) present the quantum-group graphical programme. The two inconsistent-looking q-powers in the notes cannot be repaired uniquely without those basis choices. The scanned LOMI editions carry a 1988 imprint despite their 1987 series identifiers; an exact public-circulation date before this talk is not established by that cover evidence.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The coloured link state sum and framing correction
notes: Sum products of matrix entries over spin labels on elementary diagram pieces; multiply by a q-power involving under/over counts to obtain a link invariant containing Jones's invariant.
statement: The ribbon-category evaluation gives an invariant of coloured framed oriented links. For a blackboard-framed diagram, pass to the zero-framed version by multiplying the contribution of each component coloured by j by \(\theta_j^{-w_i}\), where \(\theta_j\) is its twist scalar and \(w_i\) its signed self-writhe, in a fixed convention. An unweighted under/over count is not the required spin-dependent twist correction. The fundamental \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) colour yields the Jones invariant up to standard variable and normalization choices.
reconstruction: Framed versus ambient isotopy, signed self-writhe and colour-dependent twist are explicit repairs.
fate: \citet[\S\S5--6]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} gives the functor and link evaluation. The 1987-numbered preprint (1988 imprint) \citet{reshetikhin1987quantizedii} establishes the earlier link-invariant programme. The notebook's displayed normalization is not copied as a valid formula. The scanned LOMI editions carry a 1988 imprint despite their 1987 series identifiers; an exact public-circulation date before this talk is not established by that cover evidence.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: What does sufficiency of the SL2 invariants mean?
notes: There is a conjecture that the \(SL_2\)-invariants suffice; no object or equivalence relation follows the verb.
statement: If interpreted as separation of all oriented knot types by all colours of the Jones polynomial, the assertion is false. But the notes could instead mean recovery of another family of quantum invariants, or another weaker property; the exact conjecture is not recoverable.
reconstruction: The separation interpretation is deliberately conditional and is not entered as the original conjecture in the problem index.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{stoimenowtanaka2008mutation} constructs infinitely many pairs of hyperbolic knots with equal coloured Jones polynomials that are not mutants. The paper records a first manuscript in December 2005 and arXiv circulation in 2006; the opened version is from 2008. This refutes the explicit separation interpretation, not every possible reading of ``suffice.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the exact statement is unidentified; the most natural complete-knot-invariant interpretation has published counterexamples.

title: A rational pole ansatz and its Bethe equations
notes: The Riccati equation is \(y^{\prime}+y^2+2By+C=0\), with \(B=\sum b_\alpha\Delta(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), \(C=\sum c_\alpha\Delta(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), and \(y=\sum_i\Delta(\lambda-\lambda_i)\). The first root equation has inconsistent indices and omits a \(\Delta\).
statement: For \(\Delta(z)=1/z\), distinct fixed points and distinct roots avoiding them, the ansatz solves the equation exactly iff \(\sum_{j\ne i}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^{-1}+\sum_\alpha b_\alpha(\lambda_i-a_\alpha)^{-1}=0\) for each i and \(c_\alpha=2b_\alpha\sum_i(\lambda_i-a_\alpha)^{-1}\). Double poles cancel automatically; these conditions cancel all simple poles, and the remaining proper rational function vanishes.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The exact equivalence is deliberately restricted to the rational kernel. Other kernels require additional constant/elliptic compatibility conditions absent from the notebook.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~4, pp.~1197--1198, and \S4]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} develops the analytic pole method, referring back to the author's 1988 FIAN announcements. The residue calculation gives an exact match in the rational specialization, not an unqualified elliptic theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The addition identity and its corrected special functions
notes: For \(x+y+z=0\), \(\Delta(x)\Delta(y)+\Delta(y)\Delta(z)+\Delta(z)\Delta(x)+\Omega(x)+\Omega(y)+\Omega(z)=0\), with odd \(\Delta\) and even \(\Omega\). The trigonometric constant is printed positive and the elliptic expression lacks a half.
statement: Correct examples are \((\Delta,\Omega)=(1/z,0)\), \((\omega\cot(\omega z),-\omega^2/3)\), and \((\zeta(z),(\zeta(z)^2-\wp(z))/2)\). In the last case use \((\zeta(x)+\zeta(y)+\zeta(z))^2=\wp(x)+\wp(y)+\wp(z)\) when \(x+y+z=0\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{}
fate: The addition identity is classical; \citet[\S23.10]{nist2026dlmf} gives the Weierstrass identity. \citet[\S3 and \S11]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} places such scalar triangle identities in the quasi-exactly solvable construction. Direct substitution checks both emendations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the corrected examples satisfy the stated equation; the two literal examples do not.

title: A local Riccati identity from the addition law
notes: A solution with a singularity at zero satisfies \(\Delta^{\prime}+\Delta^2=2\Omega+\Omega(0)\).
statement: Assume \(\Delta\) is odd meromorphic with \(\Delta(t)=1/t+O(t)\), and \(\Omega\) even and holomorphic at zero. Put \(y=\varepsilon\), \(z=-x-\varepsilon\) in the addition law and let \(\varepsilon\to0\). The finite part gives exactly \(\Delta^{\prime}(x)+\Delta(x)^2=2\Omega(x)+\Omega(0)\). A different pole residue changes the derivative coefficient.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} A simple pole with residue one and regularity of \(\Omega\) at zero are indispensable extra hypotheses.
fate: The normalization argument for the constant-\(\Omega\) scalar triangle equation is given in \citet[\S3, equation~(27), p.~1197]{ushveridze1989quasiexact}. The limiting expansion supplies the displayed general form.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The claimed general kernel family is underspecified
notes: The general solution is written \(\Delta_0(b\lambda)+a\lambda\), with \(\Delta_0\) one of the rational, trigonometric or elliptic examples.
statement: A valid normalized family is obtained from a residue-one kernel by the rescaling \(b\Delta_0(b\lambda)\) and a linear addition, together with the correspondingly transformed \(\Omega\). A classification of every solution additionally requires regularity, pole and degeneracy hypotheses. The notebook neither gives these nor states the transformed \(\Omega\).
reconstruction: The prefactor b is needed only when maintaining residue one; the original unnormalized family can still satisfy an appropriately rescaled functional equation.
fate: \citet[\S3 and the final elliptic discussion in \S11]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} confirms the functional-equation method, but the retrieved review does not supply an exact theorem with the notebook's unrestricted quantifiers.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the displayed families are meaningful, but the claimed exhaustive classification is not identified precisely enough to adopt.

title: Logarithmic derivatives linearize the Riccati equation
notes: Putting \(y=f^{\prime}/f\) is said to give a Schrodinger equation; the later page writes \(f^{\prime\prime}+2Bf^{\prime}+Cf=0\).
statement: On an interval where \(f\ne0\), the substitution is equivalent to \(f^{\prime\prime}+2Bf^{\prime}+Cf=0\). Conversely, any Riccati solution gives a local nonzero f by exponentiating its integral. A gauge and coordinate change are still needed to obtain Schrodinger normal form; the first substitution alone leaves a first derivative.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The local nonvanishing condition and distinction between a linear ODE and Schrodinger normal form are explicit.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the analytic normal-form method. The equivalence follows directly from \(y^{\prime}+y^2=f^{\prime\prime}/f\).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Electrostatic interpretation of the rational roots
notes: The fixed charges are \(b_\alpha\) at \(a_\alpha\), moving charges are one at \(\lambda_i\), and the potential is written as a positive logarithm. Trigonometric and theta analogues are mentioned.
statement: For real distinct ordered roots and real fixed points, the rational Bethe equations are the stationarity equations of \(U=-\sum_{i<j}\log|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|-\sum_{i,\alpha}b_\alpha\log|\lambda_i-a_\alpha|\). Positive b produces repulsion with this sign. The logarithm of sine gives the trigonometric force; an elliptic force must use a sigma/theta logarithmic derivative with its possible linear term specified.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The real domain and sign convention are fixed. The elliptic theta kernel is not silently equated with Weierstrass zeta without its linear correction.
fate: \citet[\S5, equations~(59)--(63), pp.~1210--1212]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the electrostatic interpretation and real-interval stability assumptions. A positive logarithmic potential with minimization reverses the repulsive-energy sign.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Quantum and classical stability are not an unrestricted equivalence
notes: The same \(\lambda_i\) are called wavefunction nodes, charge positions and Bethe rapidities; quantum stability is asserted equivalent to Coulomb stability.
statement: The algebraic root equations admit these interpretations in the matched model. Spectral admissibility also depends on the Hilbert-space measure, self-adjoint domain, and endpoint behaviour. It is not equivalent merely to existence of a stationary electrostatic configuration.
reconstruction: Only the shared algebraic Bethe equations are identified; physical stability notions require separate definitions.
fate: \citet[\S5, p.~1212, comparing equations~(45)--(46) with (62)--(63)]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} explicitly says the classical and quantum interval conditions almost coincide, with shifted numerical thresholds in that paper's normalization. Thus the author's later primary account itself prevents the literal biconditional.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the model-dependent correspondence is established; the unqualified stability equivalence is false.

title: A common eigenspace yields partial exact solvability
notes: For commuting \(H_0,H_1,H_2\), form \(H=H_0+L_1(H_1-c_1)+L_2(H_2-c_2)\). Common eigenvectors with the chosen eigenvalues remain known.
statement: On a common invariant domain, let \(\mathcal V=\ker(H_1-c_1)\cap\ker(H_2-c_2)\) and suppose \(H_0\mathcal V\subset\mathcal V\). Then \(H|_{\mathcal V}=H_0|_{\mathcal V}\). In particular every known \(H_0\)-eigenvector in \(\mathcal V\) remains an H-eigenvector; no commutation of the \(L_j\) with \(H_i\) is needed. A finite-dimensional nonzero \(\mathcal V\) provides an algebraically solvable sector, not the full spectrum.
reconstruction: Domain and invariance hypotheses are supplied; self-adjointness of H is an additional analytic requirement, not automatic from the formula.
fate: \citet[\S9, equation~(113), p.~1232]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} states exactly this operator construction, in a general finite sum. The review appeared in 1989 after the FIAN work cited in the notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The nonlinear-Schrodinger and oscillator analogy
notes: Two lines compare quantum nonlinear Schrodinger theory with the harmonic oscillator, and energy with a particle-number operator; spectra are said to come from Bethe equations.
statement: The Hamiltonians, representation spaces, boundary conditions and precise correspondence are absent, so no exact spectral equivalence can be stated.
fate: \citet[\S\S7--9]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} supplies related integrable-spin and quasi-exact constructions, but does not identify these two bare correspondences as written.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: unidentified beyond the integrable-system analogy.

title: The Liouville transform to Schrodinger form
notes: Multiply by an arbitrary A, set \(x=\int d\lambda/\sqrt A\), eliminate the first derivative, and obtain a potential depending on A.
statement: On a real interval with \(A(\lambda)>0\), set \(dx/d\lambda=A^{-1/2}\), \(P=2B\sqrt A-A^{\prime}/(2\sqrt A)\), and \(\Psi=A^{-1/4}\exp(\int B\,d\lambda)f\). Then \(-\Psi_{xx}+V\Psi=0\), where \(V=\tfrac12 P_x+\tfrac14P^2-AC\). Complex versions need a local branch of \(\sqrt A\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The gauge factor, positivity/branch condition and derivatives are made explicit; a coordinate change alone does not remove the first derivative.
fate: \citet[\S2, transformation formulas leading to equation~(24)]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} develops the coordinate/gauge procedure. The displayed formula is a direct reconstruction from the notebook's equation (12).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Separating a spectral constant from the potential
notes: The product \(A=\prod_\alpha\Xi(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), \(\Xi^{\prime}/\Xi=\Delta\), is said to put all root information into an x-independent energy.
statement: For the rational kernel take A proportional to \(\prod_\alpha(\lambda-a_\alpha)\). Then \(AC\) is polynomial of degree at most \(N-2\), because the Bethe equations imply \(\sum c_\alpha=0\). For \(N=2\) it is a constant energy. For \(N>2\), additional root-dependent coefficients generally remain in the potential and must be fixed to obtain several eigenstates of one Hamiltonian.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} A nonzero scalar multiple can be chosen for positivity on the desired real interval; the source' s bare product may have negative sign there.
fate: \citet[\S4, equations~(38)--(43), pp.~1199--1201]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} distinguishes the infinitely degenerate spectral parameter from the others and makes the N-dependent distinction. The product choice alone does not prove an all-N single-energy separation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Two fixed positive charges and Jacobi polynomials
notes: For \(N=2\), \(b_1,b_2>0\), repulsion traps M particles between \(a_1<a_2\), giving a solution with M nodes for every M and an exactly solvable model.
statement: Let \(a_1<a_2\) be real, \(b_1,b_2>0\), and \(M\geq0\) an integer. On the chamber \(a_1<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_M<a_2\), the negative-log energy is strictly convex and tends to infinity at its boundary, hence has a unique minimizer. The monic polynomial \(f_M=\prod_i(\lambda-\lambda_i)\) satisfies \(Af_M^{\prime\prime}+2BAf_M^{\prime}+E_Mf_M=0\), \(A=(\lambda-a_1)(a_2-\lambda)\), \(E_M=M(M-1+2b_1+2b_2)\). Here \(B(\lambda)=b_1/(\lambda-a_1)+b_2/(\lambda-a_2)\); for M=0 the configuration is empty and \(f_0=1\). These are rescaled Jacobi polynomials, orthogonal with weight \((\lambda-a_1)^{2b_1-1}(a_2-\lambda)^{2b_2-1}\).
reconstruction: \ours{} The chosen chamber, energy sign, self-adjoint weighted realization and positive A fix the implicit analytic setup.
fate: \citet[\S4, N=2 case, and \S5]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the exactly-solvable and electrostatic interpretations. The convexity and coefficient comparison justify this precise reconstruction; physical boundary conditions after the Liouville transform must still be selected.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Exterior intervals and finitely many admissible levels
notes: For M particles to the right of the second fixed charge, the stability condition is written \(b_1+b_2+M<0\); failure for large M yields only finitely many levels.
statement: With \(b_2>0\), the displayed inequality is a sufficient confining condition for the negative-log energy on the exterior chamber, but it is not generally the sharp threshold. Already for M=1, \(a_1=0,a_2=1,b_1=-1,b_2=1/2\), \(U=\log\lambda-\tfrac12\log(\lambda-1)\) has a strict minimum at \(\lambda=2\), although \(b_1+b_2+M=1/2\). Finiteness of normalizable quantum states requires its own endpoint and measure analysis.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The counterexample only rejects necessity of the displayed condition; it does not reject that condition as a sufficient bound.
fate: \citet[\S5, equations~(62)--(63) and the following comparison, pp.~1211--1212]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} treats stable intervals and distinguishes quantum conditions. The notebook's conclusion is qualitative; no exact level count or necessary-and-sufficient bound is inferred.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: finite admissible spectra occur in the relevant models; the bare inequality is not a universal sharp quantum bound.

title: The finite-dimensional Morse complex
notes: For a compact manifold and generic metric, trajectories from \(x_1\) to \(x_2\) have dimension \(\operatorname{ind}(x_1)-\operatorname{ind}(x_2)-1\), and signed index-one trajectories define the differential. The vector field is written \(+\operatorname{grad}f\).
statement: For a Morse function on a closed manifold and a Morse--Smale metric, use the negative gradient. The unparametrized trajectory space from p to q has dimension \(\operatorname{ind}p-\operatorname{ind}q-1\). Choose orientations of unstable manifolds; signed counts for index difference one define \(d:C_i\to C_{i-1}\), with \(d^2=0\), and its homology is the ordinary homology. Mod-two coefficients avoid the orientation choices.
reconstruction: Closedness, Morse--Smale transversality, quotient by time translation and coherent orientation choices are stated explicitly.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~287--288]{atiyah1988invariants} recalls this construction after \citet[\S2]{witten1982supersymmetry}. The notebook combines positive-gradient notation with the negative-gradient index convention.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The irreducible gauge quotient
notes: The main manifold is \(X=C/G\), irreducible Hermitian connections on the trivial rank-two bundle, with \(G=SU(2)^M\).
statement: Let M be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. On the trivial \(SU(2)\)-bundle, connections form \(\mathcal A=d+\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak{su}_2)\). An irreducible connection has stabilizer the centre \(\{\pm1\}\); after Sobolev completion, the effective gauge group \(\mathcal G/\{\pm1\}\) acts freely and the quotient has local Coulomb slices. Reducible points are excluded from this manifold assertion.
reconstruction: Orientation, completion and the ineffective central stabilizer are restored.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~286--287]{atiyah1988invariants} gives precisely the irreducible quotient used in the Casson/Floer picture. The trivial-bundle condition is automatic for \(SU(2)\)-bundles over a three-dimensional CW complex, but is retained from the notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Chern--Simons one-form and its periods
notes: \(\nu_A(B)=\int_M\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge B)\) descends to the quotient and is closed. A primitive is identified with a transgression integral on \(M\times[0,1]\); Gelfand refers to Gabrielov--Gelfand--Losik.
statement: For closed oriented M, gauge invariance and the Bianchi identity make \(\nu\) basic. On \(\mathcal A\), a primitive is \(\tfrac12\int_M\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)\). Without the half, its differential is \(2\nu\). With a conventional integral normalization, large gauge transformations change the primitive by periods, so on the quotient the functional is circle-valued or defined on a covering.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The factor two and integral normalization are distinguished; the notebook suppresses both.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~287--288]{atiyah1988invariants} describes the closed one-form, the Chern--Simons functional and its integral periods. The historical Gelfand attribution is recorded as an intervention, not treated as an independent new result.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Flat critical points and the tangent quotient
notes: Critical points are flat connections, hence representations of \(\pi_1(M)\). The quotient tangent space is written with differential forms on X instead of M.
statement: The zero set of \(\nu\) consists of flat connections. Gauge-equivalence classes correspond to conjugacy classes of \(\rho:\pi_1(M)\to SU(2)\). At an irreducible connection, the tangent quotient is \(\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)/d_A\Omega^0(M;\operatorname{ad}P)\), with a Coulomb-slice realization after completion. The base of these differential forms is M, not the infinite-dimensional quotient X.
reconstruction: The notation error X is replaced by M; the tangent quotient is for the irreducible stratum.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~286--287]{atiyah1988invariants} states the flat-connection/representation correspondence; the quotient formula follows by differentiating the gauge action.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Twisted first cohomology is not ordinary homology
notes: The Hessian is \(\int_M\operatorname{tr}(d_Aa\wedge a)\). Nondegeneracy is identified with \(H^1(M;E)=0\) for every local system, and then with \(H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=0\). The Russian says \ru{Это эквивалентно}.
statement: At a specified irreducible flat connection with holonomy \(\rho\), the Hessian kernel modulo gauge is \(H^1(M;\operatorname{ad}\rho)\). An integral homology sphere need not have this group zero. Conversely, vanishing of \(H^1(M;E)\) for every finite-dimensional characteristic-zero local system does not detect integral torsion.
reconstruction: The local system governing this Hessian is the adjoint system of the chosen representation, not all local systems at once.
fate: \citet[p.~287 and p.~289]{atiyah1988invariants} explicitly requires perturbations when flat critical points are degenerate. Section~\ref{dev:twisted-h1} gives independently checked counterexamples: \(\mathbb{RP}^3\) for the reverse implication, and the connected sum of two Poincare spheres with an irreducible \(SU(2)\) representation for the forward implication.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the pointwise twisted-cohomology criterion is established; both directions of the notebook' s ordinary/twisted equivalence are false.

title: Spectral flow and the relative grading modulo eight
notes: Index difference is called the number of points where a zero mode appears, then spectral asymmetry; it is said to be well defined modulo eight.
statement: For a path of self-adjoint Fredholm gauge-fixed Hessians with nondegenerate ends, spectral flow is the signed crossing count with multiplicity (or its perturbation-invariant definition), not the unsigned number of zero events. In the \(SU(2)\) instanton theory of an integral homology sphere, changing a path by a generating gauge loop changes this index by eight; hence the relative grading descends modulo eight.
reconstruction: Signs, multiplicities, gauge fixing and the homology-sphere gauge-theory setup are required for the stated eight-periodicity.
fate: \citet[\S4, p.~289]{atiyah1988invariants} gives the spectral-flow calculation and its index-theorem origin. \citet{floer1988instanton} establishes the resulting mod-eight graded homology, received 3 May and published June 1988; only its publisher abstract, not its full proof, was read here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: A cotangent intersection recovers the Euler characteristic
notes: Take the zero section and the graph of df; intersections are critical points, with signed total written \(\chi(T^*L)\).
statement: For a closed smooth manifold L and Morse f, the zero section and \(\Gamma_{df}\) in \(T^*L\) meet transversely at the critical points. With compatible orientations the local sign is \((-1)^{\operatorname{ind}f}\), and their sum is \(\chi(L)=\chi(T^*L)\), the last equality following from deformation retraction.
reconstruction: Compactness of L, Morse nondegeneracy and the orientation convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S5]{atiyah1988invariants} uses Lagrangian intersections as the finite-dimensional model. The equality with the total-space Euler characteristic is harmless here, although the total space is noncompact.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The closed action one-form and Maslov relative index
notes: On paths from \(L_1\) to \(L_2\), define \(\nu_\gamma(\xi)=\int_0^1\omega(\dot\gamma,\xi)dt\); zeros are intersections, and a relative index is obtained from Maslov theory.
statement: Let \((N,\omega)\) be symplectic and \(L_1,L_2\) Lagrangian. The action one-form on a suitable Sobolev path space is closed because its exterior derivative is the endpoint difference of \(\omega\), which vanishes on the Lagrangians. Its zeros are constant paths in \(L_1\cap L_2\). Transverse intersections give nondegenerate Fredholm Hessians; relative grading uses the Maslov index, with ambiguity determined by the relevant loop classes. Exactness or a covering is needed for a single-valued action.
reconstruction: Lagrangian boundary conditions, Sobolev/Fredholm setup and the action-period ambiguity are explicit; existence of a full Floer homology needs further compactness hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S5, pp.~292--293]{atiyah1988invariants} describes the symplectic Floer construction and cites Floer's 1987 preprints. The index formalism has earlier variational background in \citet[\S2]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Heegaard splitting as a Lagrangian representation-space intersection
notes: A three-manifold is cut into two pieces along a surface; fundamental groups and their representations give the finite-dimensional counterpart of the connection construction.
statement: For a genus-g Heegaard splitting \(M=W_1\cup_\Sigma W_2\), each handlebody group is free of rank g and van Kampen presents \(\pi_1M\) as their amalgam over \(\pi_1\Sigma\). On the smooth irreducible locus, the \(SU(2)\) character variety of \(\Sigma\) has its cup-product symplectic form. The handlebody representation loci are Lagrangian where smooth, and their intersection represents flat connections on M. Reducibles, singularities and transversality cannot be ignored.
reconstruction: The character-variety smooth locus and Lagrangian hypotheses are supplied rather than claiming that every full representation quotient is a smooth symplectic manifold.
fate: \citet[\S5, pp.~290--293]{atiyah1988invariants} is the direct publication match. It discusses the conjectural relation of the two Floer constructions, but the notebook does not explicitly formulate that homology-isomorphism conjecture, so none is added to this year's problem index.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Instantons and cutting a four-manifold along a three-manifold
notes: Four-dimensional Yang--Mills equations and cutting a four-manifold into two three-dimensional ones are invoked as the connection to Donaldson theory.
statement: On \(M\times\mathbb R\), an anti-self-dual connection in temporal gauge satisfies \(\dot A=-*_MF_A\) for the product orientation, a Chern--Simons gradient equation after choosing the overall sign convention. A decomposition \(Z=Z_1\cup_MZ_2\) has two four-dimensional pieces sharing a three-dimensional boundary. Finite-energy instanton moduli spaces and their boundary data are the objects used in Floer/Donaldson gluing; arbitrary Yang--Mills critical points do not suffice.
reconstruction: Anti-self-duality, finite energy, temporal gauge and the dimensions of the pieces are corrected explicitly.
fate: \citet[\S4, equation~(4.1), and \S7]{atiyah1988invariants} explains the cylinder equation and the gluing programme. \citet{floer1988instanton} is the subsequent rigorous homology construction. The notebook's dimensions are a literal slip, and its analogy alone is not a complete gluing theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
